title: Why is the story always about a woman in distress?
body: Sadly, I am somewhat addicted to this game. Although energy is very hard to come by and oftentimes will take over 200 to get an item that is required to finish an order. And while it starts out with reasonable expectations of how many coins it’s going to take to make a repair, it’s up to 450 coins just to fix a plant? Plus the story is really stupid. Why would you hang curtains before you get the snow off the floor? Why wouldn’t you dress the cold people first before you adorn a plant or fill a toy box? But my pet peeve is it so far every story I’ve had is about a woman in distress. Perhaps a woman and child, perhaps a woman and pets, or perhaps a pregnant woman. It’s never a man whose truck ran off the road or who can’t find a job or is homeless. Why does it have to be so sexist?

title: Game play ok, lacking storyline
body: The merging part of the game is OK although it gets somewhat monotonous as you are essentially filling orders for customers to earn the coins and pay for improvements to the scene. Other reviewers have commented on the lack of storyline once you finish the first scene, which is completely true. I’m on the third scene and there is NO story, background or character dialogue to keep things interesting - just a scene in which you fix things. In addition, the order in which things get fixed makes absolutely zero sense… why sweep the floor and add furniture/decor when there is still a gaping hole in the roof and the rain continues to pour in? Set up the repair/restore plan in a sensible order and give it a coherent storyline, and then you’ll have a game worth playing for longer than a day or two! Deleting the app after I post this because there is nothing to keep me interested anymore.
